questions.question: Which worker style for the delegated tasks?

options.label: Headless `work start` workers
options.description: Fire-and-forget `claude -p` workers. No picker rows. I (manager) watch their logs and relay results. Best for well-scoped tasks like the emails extraction.

options.label: Picker-visible `new-session` sessions
options.description: Show up in the Claude app picker as `oneoff-*` rows. You can tap in mid-run to inspect or steer. Heavier; useful if you want to drive the worker yourself.

options.label: Mix: headless for emails, picker for SOP run
options.description: Headless for the extraction (low-touch). Picker-visible for the SOP audit so you can review findings live in Step 5 (human review window).

questions.question: Dispatch FF only now, or queue dstrader / dstrader-docker workers in parallel?

options.label: FF only — sequential by family
options.description: Match your priority order (FF → dstrader → ai-harness → dstrader-docker). Cleanest, easiest for me to manage. dstrader uses the same SOP so its worker can copy FF's pattern.

options.label: FF + dstrader in parallel
options.description: dstrader has no emails-prerequisite (no family-emails class), so its SOP run can start immediately. Saves wall-clock. Skip ai-harness (already public) and defer dstrader-docker.

options.label: All three families in parallel
options.description: FF emails worker + FF SOP (chained), dstrader SOP, dstrader-docker SOP all kicked off. Maximum throughput; harder to track.
